newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China city party boss slams listed loss-makers.
newsitem.headline: China city party boss slams listed loss-makers.

text.p: The Communist Party chief in China's southern city of Shenzhen has lashed out at loss-making state-owned listed firms, saying their executives should be fired, the Securities Times said on Wednesday.
Leaders of state-owned listed companies incurring heavy losses should be purged and possibly sued, the newspaper quoted Shenzhen party secretary Li Youwei as saying at a recent government meeting.
"Li severely criticised some loss-making state enterprises and listed firms in which the state holds a controlling stake," the Shenzhen paper said.
Li also urged companies to stop investments that were not backed by adequate feasibility studies, it said.
Some 31 companies out of more than 500 listed in mainland China posted losses for 1996, the newspaper said.
China's state-owned firms have struggled to cope with nearly two decades of economic reform that have pushed the nation towards a market economy.
Some 75 percent of China's more than 100,000 state-owned enterprises are in the red, with 40 percent suffering chronic deficits, official figures show.
